summary: Learn transaction testing, fraud red flags, Excel analysis, Power BI dashboards, and investigation workflows. Explore the course and request details.
lede: Fraud analytics helps finance, audit, compliance, and investigation professionals examine transaction data for irregularities that merit review. The training covers preparing and validating files in Excel, testing duplicate payments, split transactions, payroll and claims exceptions, and organizing red flags with the ACFE Fraud Tree. Learners also practice designing Power BI exception dashboards and documenting alert triage, evidence, and control follow-up; AI-assisted monitoring is covered conceptually, with human review emphasized.
audienceIntro: This fraud analytics course suits professionals who examine financial transactions, assess fraud controls, or investigate exceptions across finance operations. It is designed for roles that need to turn data irregularities into documented, proportionate follow-up. This course is designed for: Internal auditors testing payment, procurement, payroll, and claims controls. Forensic accountants tracing unusual transaction patterns and documenting evidence. Fraud analysts screening transactions and prioritizing exceptions for review. Finance managers monitoring payment approvals, supplier records, and payroll anomalies. Compliance officers assessing fraud controls and escalation documentation. Corporate investigators developing transaction leads into structured case inquiries. Accounts payable supervisors reviewing duplicate invoices and unusual payment changes. Procurement assurance specialists testing supplier selection and purchase-order exceptions. Payroll auditors identifying unusual employee payments and master-file changes. Claims examiners reviewing claim patterns and referrals for further investigation.
prerequisites: Prerequisites: Working familiarity with finance transactions, audit, compliance, or investigations is recommended. Basic Excel use will help you complete the data-preparation exercises. No programming is required. The course treats AI-assisted monitoring and advanced statistical techniques at conceptual-awareness level, not implementation level.
